Honestly, I never thought the day would come when EA would release their titles on Steam, even if they still require Origin, like how Ubisoft titles on Steam work, requiring Uplay.
For starters, that means a lot of “new” games got released on Steam, and EA deserves some praise for that, even if it took them almost a decade.
Secondly, and for Mass Effect 3 specifically, now you can finally own and play the entire Mass Effect Trilogy on Steam, something that I ranted about in the previous games, because for me Mass Effect should be played as a trilogy, especially with some many choices that you can import from the first game to the second and now to the third. It truly feels like a single giant game released in 3 standalone parts.
Well, technically you still can only own most of the Mass Effect 2 DLC on Origin, although you can install it on Steam manually and play it there without problems. So, I can kind of give it a pass on that one. Thankfully, you can get the complete version of Mass Effect 3 on Steam, although it’s overpriced given its age.
Now, is Mass Effect 3 worth it? First, as I said before, I don’t recommend jumping straight to Mass Effect 3. You should start with the original, (although it hasn’t aged well), then 2, if you can with all DLCs, then finally 3. If you enjoyed Mass Effect 2, you’re definitely going to enjoy Mass Effect 3.
For the most part, Mass Effect 3 plays similarly to Mass Effect 2. Gameplay is similar, with some rebalancing considering that now it also includes a multiplayer mode. But it’s almost dead now, and I didn’t touch it, so my opinion is only valid for the single player experience. Still, it’s a nice addition, although it already included microtransactions, even back in 2012.
Perhaps the biggest difference is in the story and it’s scope. Mass Effect 2 was focused on recruiting and bonding with your crew. This time it’s about an epic galactic war, where you aid the various alien races, and get resources to help create the only weapon that can defeat the enemy forces. It also brings closure to some of the biggest lore plots, like the Genophage and the war between the Quarians and the Geth.
And, of course, once again, most choices are up to you. You can be a Paragon hero, or a Renegade jackass (still worth a playthrough for that, the Renegade options are way funnier). After so many different endings in Mass Effect 2, I wondered how they would manage to fit all those choices in this game. Well, mostly they took the lazy route, bringing mainly characters that had minor roles in Mass Effect 2 or none at all, and replacing dead crewmates roles with way less interesting NPCs. Really, try to import a Mass Effect 2 save with most if not all of your past crew members alive, you’ll have a better experience. Anyway, it was hard doing better than they did. You can even see the impact of some choices from Mass Effect 1.
Graphics are slightly improved, and the soundtrack is good as usual. What the game does best is making you feel that you are in the middle of an epic galactic war. The original ending sucked so much that a free DLC got released with an extended version. While still a bit disappointing, it’s a big improvement over the original. The main problem is that for a huge trilogy focused on player choice, most of them just translate to resources, affecting your ending options and some slightly different scenes in there. However, don’t forget the plot closures, that act as semi-endings of some sort.
If we are just talking about the main game, I still slightly prefer Mass Effect 2. However, Mass Effect 3 has one of the best DLCs in videogame history, and if we include that then it easily ties with Mass Effect 2. That DLC is Citadel, and it has everything that a final game in a trilogy like this should have: a lighthearted story focused on comedy to give us some change, an amazing party with all alive crew members that you prepare and throw, with plenty of interactions (the best part) and even an arena for more replayability with end game combat, if that’s you thing, with more squad mates joining you for those battles. And the more you are invested in this universe and it’s characters, the better it will be. It’s just that good.
So, I’m not going to recommend Mass Effect 3 as a standalone game, but the whole trilogy, since that’s how it was designed to be played, from the beginning of the first game to the ending of the third. It’s one of my favorite trilogies/game, and even if it’s still a bit overpriced for the age, I think it’s worth it if you enjoy deep narrative experiences.
By the way, if you already own the game on Origin, and want to have it on Steam, you’ll need to buy it again, which I think was expected. You can also buy a bundle with all DLCs on Steam, however, if you already bought them on Origin, you can play them on the Steam version. Technically you don’t own them on Steam, but the Origin client will download them automatically to the Steam folder and you can play them without any problem. That was another thing that surprised me, but considering the price of this older game, I won’t praise it that much. Another nice touch they included was automatically unlocking your Origin achievements on Steam. So, you don’t need to play the game again to 100% if you’re a completionist and just want to have the achievements unlocked on Steam.

EA coming back home to Steam still expects you to buy DLCs for 9 years old game, not forgetting to include the [b] FREE [/b] DLC packs for multiplayer in the paid bundle. Just wait it out and maybe get the remastered trilogy if you want all in one package.
============================================================
DLCs were added to the legacy edition, we are so back!

PROS:
- The world of Mass Effect 3 is immersive. If you compare this game to its predecessors, this game's atmosphere and world takes the cake.
- A lot of the main cast have become more well-rounded. The character development of this game is not as good as 2's but still great.
- Main missions are amazing to play.
- Enemies (the ground troopers of the reapers) have great designs, and have a lot of variations. The other ground troopers (namely Cerberus troops) are also well-designed.
- Love interest conversations are better than 1 and 2.
- Combat has been overhauled and is an all-around great experience.
- Shepard is still a badass
- The fan service is there, but is implemented well.

CONS:
- The journal is a mess, most of the time the journal doesn't even help you find where you need to go.
- A lot of the NPC conversations will repeat after you've already heard it (especially on the Citadel)
- Ending is still a touchy subject. 
- An early softlock is present 
- A few game-breaking bugs made me reload a save or restart a mission. 

DLC integration is easier than the previous titles, because the DLC for Mass Effect 3 is on the Steam store.
Hope you enjoy the game, fellow N7s.
